sentences.text: Dated this the 10th day of July, 2025  ORDER
This bail application is filed under Section 482 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (for short 'BNSS').

2. Petitioners are accused Nos.2 to 4 in Crime No.1227/2024 of Ollur Police Station, Thrissur District; registered for the offences punishable under Sections 406 and 420 r/w Section 34 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860.

3. The prosecution case is that the first accused, M/s.Pooram Nidhi Ltd., accepted deposit to the tune of Rs.2,00,000/- from the defacto complainant pursuant to the inducement of accused Nos.2 to 4, who are its Directors, and thereafter failed to pay any interest or return the amount of investment and thus committed the offences alleged.
4.
Smt.Anupama Subramanian, the learned counsel for the petitioners submitted that the entire prosecution allegations are false and there was no dishonest intention at all.

She further submitted that due to Covid-19 Pandemic, various receivables of the Company could not be recovered, and several persons defaulted on their repayments, as a result of which, petitioners could not cater to the interest payments on the deposits BAIL APPL. NO. 7890 OF 2025 2025:KER:50747 accepted by them.

The learned counsel pointed out that various civil suits have been filed to recover amounts due to the petitioners, and in the absence of any dishonest intention from the very beginning, the C.K. Anilkumar vs State Of Kerala on 10 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/89599745/
2 offence itself is not made out.
5.

sentences.text: Smt.Sreeja V., the learned Public Prosecutor opposed the bail application and submitted that petitioners are involved in 30 other crimes, and unless custodial interrogation is permitted, the investigation will be prejudiced.
6. I have considered the rival contentions.

7. Prosecution allegations indicate that the first accused, which is a Company, had accepted deposits from the defacto complainant to the tune of Rs.2,00,000/- promising to pay interest and return the principal amount on maturity.
However, despite maturity of the deposit, the same has not been returned nor has the interest been paid.

Though the allegations are serious, considering the circumstances pointed out by the learned counsel for the petitioners, I am of the view that custodial interrogation of the petitioners is not necessary.

8. In this context it is appropriate to refer to the decision in Ashok Kumar v. State of Union Territory Chandigarh [2024 SCC OnLine SC 274], wherein it has been held that a mere assertion on the part of the State while opposing the plea for anticipatory bail that custodial interrogation is required would not be sufficient and that the State would have to show or indicate more than prima facie case as to why custodial interrogation BAIL APPL. NO. 7890 OF 2025 2025:KER:50747 of the accused is required for the purpose of investigation.
9.

entities.text: Ashok Kumar v. State of Union Territory Chandigarh [2024 SCC OnLine SC 274]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the instant case, the State has not been able to convince this Court that custodial interrogation is necessary.
Considering the nature of allegations, I am of the view that custodial interrogation of the petitioners is not necessary.
However, petitioners must subject themselves to interrogation for the purpose of completing the investigation.

10. Accordingly, this application is allowed on the following conditions:
(a) Petitioners shall appear before the Investigating Officer on 28.07.2025 and shall subject themselves to interrogation.

(b) If after interrogation, the Investigating Officer proposes to arrest the petitioners, then, they shall be released on bail on each of them executing a bond for Rs.50,000/- (Rupees fifty thousand only)
with two solvent sureties each for the like sum before the Investigating Officer.
(c) Petitioners shall appear before the Investigating Officer as and when required and shall also co-operate with the investigation.

(d) Petitioners shall not intimidate or attempt to influence the witnesses; nor shall they tamper with the evidence;
(e) Petitioners shall not commit any similar offences while they are on bail.
